direction: Use a Gram-matrix rank-relaxation to generate genuinely new basins: starting from random symmetric matrices and from the incumbent Gram matrix, alternately project onto (i) unit diagonal and off-diagonal entries capped at a trial target $t$, (ii) positive-semidefinite matrices by eigenvalue clipping, and (iii) rank at most 22 by retaining the 22 largest eigenvalues, for $t=0.064,0.060,0.055$ and 200–500 cheap NumPy iterations per trial. Factor each resulting Gram matrix as $X=V\sqrt{\Lambda}$, normalize its rows, score it exactly, and give only the best few factors a short 2,000-step annealed LSE-Adam polish. Keep the incumbent as a fallback and impose a strict internal deadline of about 150 seconds; this searches over Gram/contact patterns inaccessible to point-space perturbations of the record.

idea: Jammed-basin escape via alternating Gaussian hops and worst-point largest-empty-cap kill-and-fill, interleaved with annealed soft-max Riemannian Adam and high-beta L-BFGS polishing.

Cardinality continuation both ways — delete highest-contact point to 58 and re-insert at optimized largest empty cap, plus overcomplete 60/61 polish with greedy deletion — using short annealed LSE/hard polishes with fallback.
direction: Apply cardinality continuation in both directions: create a 58-point problem by deleting a highest-contact point and polishing it to a substantially lower maximum, locate the largest empty spherical cap by batched random sampling plus local maximization of the minimum angle to the 58 points, insert a new point there, and jointly re-polish all 59 points; in parallel, optimize 60- and 61-point overcomplete configurations from perturbed copies, iteratively delete the point with the largest row-maximum/contact load, and re-polish after each deletion down to 59 points. The easier 58-point geometry and the overcomplete $60/61$-point geometry have different jamming and contact structures, so insertion/deletion can land in a new 59-point basin; run only a handful of Adam-polished cycles, always preserve the loaded best as fallback, and terminate by about 150 seconds to avoid previous timeout failures.

Break the jammed contact graph with forced-facet LP moves that drive random dominant-contact subsets 2e-4 below the incumbent while capping other rises, followed by short Adam polishes.
direction: Use LP duality and forced contact-breaking: build a tangent basis for each point and solve, with `scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs")`, the trust-region LP minimizing $t$ subject to linearized pair constraints for pairs within $10^{-5}$ of the maximum; use the LP marginals/equilibrium stresses, or randomized subsets when marginals are unavailable, to select 20–50 dominant contacts, then re-solve a sequence of 5–10 relinearized LPs requiring those selected cosines to fall at least $2\times10^{-4}$ below the incumbent maximum while allowing the others to rise by no more than $10^{-4}$. Follow each forced-facet move with a short Adam polish, trying several random stress/contact subsets under a firm clock limit. This deliberately sacrifices the current perfectly tied contact graph instead of returning to its nearest LP optimum.

direction: Perform cooperative multi-point deletion and reinsertion rather than single-point moves: repeatedly remove $k=4$–$7$ points, chosen randomly or among the highest-contact points, freeze the remaining points, and sample batches of 20,000 random unit vectors to find directions minimizing the maximum cosine to the frozen set; greedily insert the removed points one at a time with mutual repulsion, then optimize only the inserted points plus their 10–15 nearest neighbours with LSE-Adam before a brief full polish. Because several mutually interacting points move together, this can cross barriers that defeat rattler replacement—there are no rattlers—and batched matrix products keep each attempt to a few seconds. Track time every batch, retain the best exact configuration, and stop all trials by 145 seconds.

idea: Escape the jammed basin with overloaded-subset shakes and worst-point kill-and-fill hole reinsertion, each followed by short annealed soft-max Adam to form a new topology.
Deletion-split homotopy plus 23D lift-project basin change with staged low-to-high beta LSE Adam.
direction: Reach a new basin by homotopy in point number and dimension, especially point splitting. First delete in turn each point (or just the ten highest-contact points), quickly polish the resulting 58-point codes, and keep the best; optimise that easier 58-point problem more thoroughly, then restore 59 points by splitting a selected $x_k$ into $\mathrm{normalize}(x_k\pm\varepsilon t)$, where $t$ is a random tangent vector or a direction found from a large empty spherical cap and $\varepsilon\in[0.03,0.2]$. In parallel, try a dimensional route: embed the record in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$ with small random extra coordinates, optimise there where extra freedom can untie contacts, gradually penalise or rotate away the last coordinate, project back to $\mathbb{R}^{22}$, and repolish. Staged LSE annealing (low beta to move the split pair apart, then beta increasing to $500$--$1000$) should be used, with each deletion/split variant time-boxed to roughly 20--40 seconds and the incumbent best always preserved.

idea: LP-guided surgical basin escape from the jammed optimum using tangent-space rigidity LPs and dual-stress contact breaking followed by fast annealed Adam repolish.
direction: Use rigidity and LP duality to choose which contact to break instead of perturbing blindly. Build per-point tangent bases (59 bases of size $22\times21$), construct the sparse rigidity matrix for pairs within, say, $10^{-4}$ of the maximum, and solve one sparse HiGHS LP at a time: minimise $t$ subject to the linearised contact constraints $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle+\langle u_i,x_j\rangle+\langle u_j,x_i\rangle\le t$ and a small trust region such as $\|u\|_\infty\le10^{-3}$. If the LP predicts $t$ below the current maximum, take the step with backtracking; if it certifies local optimality, extract a nonnegative self-stress from the dual and identify the most heavily stressed or most redundant contacts. Then forbid one such contact by requiring it to rise at least $10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$ above the current maximum or by deleting its endpoints from each other's active set, resolve/repolish, and allow the remaining contacts to fall. Run at most a few dozen such LP-guided topology changes, each with strict time checks, so the LP is a surgical escape tool rather than the slow main optimiser.

idea: Frozen-context cluster excision testing new contact topologies by reinserting hub neighbourhoods from a scored random pool with subset-only annealed optimization before full unfreezing.
direction: Perform targeted cluster excision with a frozen context, not single-rattler moves (there are none). Repeatedly choose a high-contact point and 5--9 of its contact-graph neighbours, freeze the remaining 50--53 points, and reinsert the removed points one at a time: score a precomputed pool of at least 20,000 random unit vectors by their maximum inner product with the frozen set (one matrix multiplication), take the best 100 candidates for each vacancy, locally optimise only the reinserted points against the frozen set with 300--500 annealed LSE-Adam steps, and then unfreeze everything for a short 1,500-step polish. Cycle through several clusters and accept a move only if the fully polished maximum improves; enforce an internal 160-second deadline, check time every 50 iterations, and always retain the best complete configuration encountered. Freezing most variables makes each topology change cheap enough to test many clusters, unlike previous sequential kill-and-fill implementations that timed out.

idea: Cluster-subset basin hopping with worst-point kill-and-fill hole reinsertion and annealed LogSumExp Adam to escape the fully-jammed basin into a new contact topology.
Alternate 58→59 delete-polish-hole-fill and 63→59 overshoot-polish-prune cycles to force contact-topology changes with batched large-hole search and short annealed soft-max Adam re-polish.
direction: Use continuation in the number of points, inserting into a relaxed code and pruning from an overcrowded code to force topology changes. For the deletion path, remove the highest-contact point to obtain a 58-point code, polish it until its maximum is appreciably below the 59-point value, locate the largest spherical hole with 30,000--50,000 batched random candidates followed by single-point tangent refinement, insert that point as the new 59th point, and jointly re-polish. For the overshoot path, create 61--64 points by adding hole candidates or splitting highly contacted points into two slightly separated copies, polish the overcrowded system briefly, delete the point whose removal most reduces the maximum (estimated from its largest few cosines), and re-polish after each deletion until 59 points remain. Alternate these $58\to59$ and $63\to59$ cycles with modest Adam schedules and best-ever tracking under a strict time budget; changing $N$ changes the feasible contact topology in a way that fixed-$N$ shaking of the jammed 59-point configuration cannot.

idea: Greedy max-min selection from D22, coordinate and random pools followed by annealed Riesz and log-sum-exp Adam to find a sparse-contact basin, keeping the polished record as fallback.
direction: Search for an entirely different basin from structured algebraic seeds instead of perturbing the record. Construct candidate pools such as the $924$ normalised $D_{22}$ minimal vectors $(\pm1,\pm1,0,\ldots,0)/\sqrt2$, signed coordinate vectors supplemented by normalised pair sums, and greedy max-min subsets selected from large random spherical samples; from each pool select 59 points by batched greedy minimisation of the current maximum cosine. Optimise these independent seeds first with a Riesz-type repulsion energy $\sum_{i<j}((1+\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)/2)^p$ annealed through $p=4,16,64$ and then with annealed log-sum-exp Adam, discarding basins that collapse back to an extremely dense, uniform contact graph. Polish only the best two or three structurally distinct outcomes (measured by maximum cosine, number of pairs within $10^{-3}$ of the maximum, and contacts per point) and return the best configuration found; this seeks the missing sparse-contact, slack-heterogeneous topology globally rather than assuming it is reachable by a small deformation of the record.

idea: Escape the jammed equioscillated basin with worst-point kill-and-hole-reinsertion, subset shakes and fresh random restarts interleaved with fast annealed LogSumExp Riemannian Adam and greedy single-point hill climbing.
Frozen-subset deletion of high-contact points with greedy optimal hole reinsertion and masked-then-full annealed Adam polish.
direction: Artificially create rattlers by frozen-subset deletion and optimal hole reinsertion. Repeatedly delete $k\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ points chosen among the highest-contact points of the current best, freeze the remaining $59-k$ points, and generate about 20,000 unit candidates in batches from Gaussian samples, normalised sums/differences of frozen points, and local perturbations of the largest-hole candidates. Score candidates by their maximum cosine against the frozen set, greedily insert them one at a time while also accounting for cosines among inserted points, then optimise only the inserted rows for roughly 800 tangent Adam steps with gradients for frozen rows masked to zero. After insertion, unfreeze everything for a short 1500--2500-step annealed Adam polish and retain the result only if the true maximum improves; this directly manufactures the slack and low-contact points absent from the current solution, changes which pairs can become contacts, and is much cheaper and more robust than repeatedly solving a full trust-region LP.

idea: Alternate N-continuation cycles that delete the highest-contact point to 58, polish the relaxed code, reinsert the refined largest spherical hole, and overshoot to 62-63 by hole insertion plus splitting jammed points then greedily prune back to 59 with annealed soft-max Adam.
direction: Use continuation in the number of points, inserting into a relaxed code and pruning from an overcrowded code to force topology changes. For the deletion path, remove the highest-contact point to obtain a 58-point code, polish it until its maximum is appreciably below the 59-point value, locate the largest spherical hole with 30,000--50,000 batched random candidates followed by single-point tangent refinement, insert that point as the new 59th point, and jointly re-polish. For the overshoot path, create 61--64 points by adding hole candidates or splitting highly contacted points into two slightly separated copies, polish the overcrowded system briefly, delete the point whose removal most reduces the maximum (estimated from its largest few cosines), and re-polish after each deletion until 59 points remain. Alternate these $58\to59$ and $63\to59$ cycles with modest Adam schedules and best-ever tracking under a strict time budget; changing $N$ changes the feasible contact topology in a way that fixed-$N$ shaking of the jammed 59-point configuration cannot.

idea: Escape the jammed basin along near-null modes of the contact Jacobian with null-projected random combinations and short annealed log-sum-exp Adam re-polish.
direction: Escape along near-null modes of the contact Jacobian rather than along random noise or an LP. Load and normalise `best.npy`, retain it as the guaranteed fallback, form the active set $A=\{(i,j):\langle x_i,x_j\rangle>m-10^{-4}\}$, and build its tangent Jacobian, whose $(i,j)$ row contains $x_j-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_i$ in block $i$ and the symmetric term in block $j$. Compute the 20--40 smallest right singular vectors with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds` (or a randomised SVD on the ambient $ |A|\times1298$ Jacobian), reshape each mode to $(59,22)$, project it onto the tangent spaces, and try signed displacements $\varepsilon\in\{0.01,0.03,0.1,0.2\}$ followed by renormalisation; these moves preserve almost all contacts to first order while breaking their exact tie pattern. Re-polish each promising displaced point with only 600--1200 steps of the existing vectorised annealed log-sum-exp Adam ($\beta:100\to600$), keep the best-ever configuration, cycle over active thresholds $10^{-3},10^{-4},10^{-5}$ and fresh random combinations of the low modes, and enforce a hard internal deadline near 150 seconds so no SVD or polish can cause the previous timeout failures.

idea: Metropolis ruin-and-recreate basin hopping that removes the worst jammed cluster and greedily reinserts it into large spherical holes, then re-polishes with annealed soft-max Riemannian Adam while tracking the global best.

Escape the jammed equioscillated basin with cooperative rigid-cap moves (coherent shifts and hemisphere twists that preserve intra-subset distances) plus large multi-point hole reinsertion from diverse random and heavily perturbed seeds, followed by annealed soft-max Adam and L-BFGS squeezing.
